sections.heading: Label Adaptivity in Best-of-n Budget Selection
sections.text:
Rong He | 2026-10-01 | Preprint · Zenodo v1

How should a best-of-n deployment budget be chosen from a fixed candidate pool with limited correctness labels? This work gives matching minimax expected-regret bounds for adaptive and non-adaptive labelling. The extra logarithmic cost of non-adaptivity affects only the label term. The bounds account for pool size, label budget and menu width. Exact checks and synthetic diagnostics illustrate finite-budget limits; they do not establish gains on real tasks.

sections.heading: From Pointwise Queries to Population Probabilities: A Sharp Preservation Threshold
sections.text:
Rong He | 2026-09-28 | Preprint · Zenodo v1.0

Compares a finite menu of Boolean queries that return either a truth value at an unknown state or an exact population probability. For pointwise minimax error e and population minimax excess zero-one risk R, proves e ≤ R ≤ 2e. Equality is universally preserved when e = 0 or e ≥ 1/3; every attainable error between 0 and 1/3 admits an interface with R > e. The result concerns exact, restricted query interfaces, not model performance.

sections.heading: Decomposition Buys Integrity, Not Yield
sections.text:
Rong He | 2026-09-15 | Preprint · arXiv v1

Studies what task decomposition buys and loses: smaller root context, but less of the information discovered by leaves surviving the journey back. Models retention as r(b) = 1/b, validates it on 20,000 irregular trees, and analyses 600 production deep-research traces and 743,819 tool calls. Flat structures are optimal for yield; decomposition earns its keep through context integrity and cost.

sections.heading: Prefix Sharing Is a Sorting Problem
sections.text:
Rong He | 2026-09-12 | Preprint · arXiv v1

Recasts the ordering of reusable prompt chunks as a binary-hierarchy problem over requests, identifying when a fixed global order is suboptimal. On BM25 retrieval traces from three BEIR corpora, the layout reduces prefill computation by 17–36% compared with production RAG ordering.

sections.heading: Sharp Limits on Time-Reversal Detection in Binary Hidden Markov Models
sections.text:
Rong He | 2026-09-10 | Preprint · Zenodo v0.10

Constructs stationary binary hidden Markov models with strictly positive transitions and emissions whose observations conceal the direction of time at any 2n − 4 sampling instants. Establishes a matching, sharp sample-complexity bound for detection.
